“Congress may be down but certainly not out”, remarked Punjab Congress chief, Captain Amarinder Singh after the party faced a drubbing in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Assam elections. Captain Amarinder might have tried to put a brave front but an all time low performance of the party has hit the morale of party workers in Punjab unit of Congress to its lowest ebb.

Sitting on opposition bench for more than nine years, Congress party is trying hard to emerge from ashes after its back to back defeat in elections in 2007 and 2012. It is do or die battle for Captain Amarinder Singh who was given the charge of state leadership despite suffering two successive defeats under his leadership. The central leadership might have pinned high hopes on Captain Amarinder, but huge problems galore faction ridden Congress party in Punjab.

Congress spin-doctors tried to present a rosy picture by highlighting the fact the party had retained number two position in three states but the worries of an average party worker had only mounted, as it appeared to be a nationwide sentiment against the grand old party. With assembly elections in Punjab less than eight months away, the Congress had set high hopes from state and hoping to turn the tide in its favour. But, instead, the state unit of Congress seems to be in self-destruction mode. Congress is desperate to wrest power from ruling SAD-BJP government and vice-president Rahul Gandhi had focused his attention on Punjab. Congress’ desperation could be gauged from the fact that the high command had succumbed to pressure built up over the last couple of years for a change in the state leadership. Former chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh had waged an open battle against state Congress chief Partap Singh Bajwa for nearly three years. Rahul Gandhi is known for taking drastic moves and early this year he made close confidante and former union minister Ambika Soni in charge of the election campaign committee. Rahul might have taken this move with an effort to strengthen the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee but it didn’t go down well with Amarinder Singh and Rahul had to finally retract from his decision.

Once again Gandhi gave up in front of Captain Amarinder and took up his suggestion to recruit well-known election strategist Prashant Kishor to guide the party’s campaign in the state. Prashant is credited with devising the victorious strategy of Narendra Modi in general election in 2014 and most recently helping Nitish Kumar scoring his third scusseive victory. But, Punjab Congress is a different ball game all together and Prashant faces a upheavel task of steering the factionalism led party in Punjab.

Leadership was never an issue with Modi and Nitish Kumar but Congress is a different cup of tea altogether. While Rahul was initially hesitant to sign up Prashnat for Punjab election, the party even went on to take him on board for upcoming UP elections.

Captain Amarinder was so enamoured with the skills of Kishor that he went all out to ensure that Congress rope him in for Punjab elections. However, it doesn’t seem a smooth ride for either of them in Punjab and cracks are visible with Captain Amarinder not inclined to blindly follow the diktat of Prashant.

In barely two months since Prashant has come on board, major points of disagreement have surfaced between two. Both Captain and Prashant have went on record to express their dissent and differences with each other. While Captain directed Prashant to stick to his brief and not to interfare in party matters, Prashant on the other hand hinted of parting ways with Congress if he was not given free hand.

The difference between two arose when Captain decided to embark upon one month trip to US. Although Prashant was against his move, the consensus between them was reached as Captain decided to shorten his trip by one week. The disagreement between the two took an ugly shape when Prashant met the expelled leaders Bir Davinder Singh and Jagmeet Singh Brar with an aim to placate them.

While Captain has so far failed to galavanise the Congress party, the growing differnces with Prashant Kishor is denting the future propects of the party in state. The party is yet to channelise all its energies to fight its opponents for Punjab elections and has instead been busy fire-fighting internally.
